findings.claim: T133-MIN: Within the declared OC verdict class, each promoted tuple component is required by a verdict-changing witness pair.
findings.failure_mode: The finite evaluator accepts T133-MIN by checking syntactic fields such as required_components, dropped_component, and changed_fields. It does not evaluate full keep/drop OC tuples against an independent declared verdict function, so the finite case is self-confirming and does not establish a semantic verdict-changing witness pair.
findings.required_repair: Implement explicit keep/drop tuple objects and an independent OC verdict evaluator in the finite runner; require keep=ACCEPT and drop=REJECT for each component; add a negative control where changed_fields is syntactically correct but the verdict does not change, and require rejection.

findings.claim: T133-KLEVEL: Every adjacent K-level transition K0->K12 has a witness, a reduction-failure criterion, and a lawful demotion criterion.
findings.failure_mode: The Lean proof constructs TransitionEvidence by enum case and arithmetic witnessCode=upperCode*100+7, then proves existence from those fields. The finite runner mirrors the same code/flag checks. Neither artifact models lower/upper K semantics, an actual reduction map, equivalence preservation, or a verdict-changing witness pair, so K-level irreducibility is asserted rather than tested.
findings.required_repair: Encode each adjacent transition as lower model, upper model, added-axis observable, reduction attempt, and verdict comparison; prove reduction failure from the model semantics and prove lawful demotion only when the same semantic witness is absent or observationally inert.

findings.claim: T133-OMEGA-STATUS: Live status, death, residue, and rebirth are distinct typed predicates and morphism classes.
findings.failure_mode: The promoted Lean ref declared_death_blocks_live only derives contradiction from simultaneously assuming L.live x=false and L.live x=true after death. It does not prove live, death, residue, and rebirth are non-interchangeable typed predicates/classes, and the finite case reduces the distinction to booleans and string inequality.
findings.required_repair: Add Lean definitions for status predicates and residue/rebirth morphism classes with explicit disjointness/non-interchangeability theorems; bind the finite cases to those definitions instead of string/boolean field tests.

findings.claim: All promoted theorem rows are traceable through theorem -> Lean subset -> semantic finite witness.
findings.failure_mode: The canonical lean_ref in the theorem inventory does not consistently match the finite witness lean_ref. For example T133-K-ZERO points to zero_cause_has_cause in the inventory while finite checks use k_zero_iff_declared_zero_cause; T133-BOUNDARY points to metric_boundary_is_classifier while finite checks use metric_boundary_failure_equiv. A hostile reader cannot tell which theorem is actually load-bearing.
findings.required_repair: Make each theorem_id have one canonical load-bearing Lean theorem, or add an explicit supporting_lean_refs array with roles; update proof ledger and finite inputs so every finite case names the same canonical theorem or a declared sublemma.

findings.claim: OC133-NOSEND-001: Publication and journal submission remain locked until separate owner approval.
findings.failure_mode: The owner-approved control row cites releases/oc_core_1_3_3/editorial/OWNER_RELEASE_APPROVAL_v1.3.3.json as its lean_ref but embeds owner_approved=true and publish_allowed=true, while the current referenced approval/manifest artifacts are pending/false. The runner accepts the inline model without reading the referenced artifact, so the no-send finite case is not artifact-grounded.
findings.required_repair: Make the runner load and compare the referenced manifest/approval JSON fields. If an approved control is needed, put it in a separate synthetic fixture clearly marked as hypothetical rather than citing the current pending approval artifact.

findings.claim: Phenomenon rows are PHENOMENON_SPECIFIC_MODEL_REPLAYED and route claim -> theorem -> semantic finite case -> falsifier.
findings.failure_mode: The falsifier text is generic boilerplate across rows rather than a concrete executable falsifier. Broad phenomena such as origin-of-life framing, social institutions, and release governance are marked replayed by toy model cards. P012 also claims a Lean theorem/proof-sheet route for OC133-NOSEND-001 even though no no-send theorem appears in the theorem inventory.
findings.required_repair: For each phenomenon row, add a concrete falsifier case ID, exact input mutation, expected runner rejection, and domain boundary. Demote rows that only have a toy replay, and remove theorem/proof-sheet route language where no theorem exists.

findings.claim: critical_unresolved_total=0 and high_unresolved_total=0 for the total attack matrix.
findings.failure_mode: Critical/high attacks are closed by token presence checks such as semantic_evaluator=true, NOT_PROMOTED_PRIOR_ART_POSITIONING_ONLY, PHENOMENON_SPECIFIC_MODEL_REPLAYED, publish_allowed=false, or theorem-name strings. These closures do not verify the attacked failure mode and often close self-confirming-finite-model or relabeling attacks with the artifact under attack.
findings.required_repair: Reopen closures whose verification query is only a status token or theorem name. Require issue-specific closure evidence that inspects the linked claim, theorem, finite input, observed verdict, negative control, and falsifier; remove duplicated generated attack rows or mark them non-independent.

findings.claim: Numeric rows provide replay QA with baseline negative-control falsifiers.
findings.failure_mode: The table contains asserted predicted/observed values and prose negative controls, but no executable replay command, raw snapshot hashes, parser output, or observed negative-control verdicts. A hostile reader cannot distinguish executed replay QA from hand-entered numbers.
findings.required_repair: Add an executable numeric replay ledger with command, script hash, raw snapshot hashes, parsed observed values, residual calculation, comparator calculation, negative-control input, and negative-control observed verdict for each row; demote rows until those fields exist.

findings.claim: OC133-NOVELTY-001: Prior-art comparison supports bounded positioning of the OC release-governance bundle; uniqueness is not promoted.
findings.failure_mode: The register repeatedly uses NOT_FOUND_IN_SOURCE_PAGE or source-page absence tests as residual-delta evidence. That is too weak even for bounded positioning because it does not search adjacent release-governance, V&V, artifact-evaluation, registered-report, model-card, or formal-methods control-plane prior art.
findings.required_repair: Rename the current register as anchor-only positioning, or add systematic comparator rows for adjacent governance and formal-method traditions with explicit overlap tests before using source-backed positioning language.
